positive_controls.argument: Maintained interface rationale and constraints let later teams interpret shared commitments without reconstructing tacit agreement.
Authoritative component and system identities make coordinated commitments refer to a particular recoverable configuration.
Observed drift and deployment differences expose commitments that coordinated teams must repair or explicitly renegotiate.
Risk-proportional authority and change analysis determine which cross-team commitments need consultation, approval or updated evidence.
A testable versioned contract makes the coordinated commitment concrete and distinguishes local freedom from externally consequential changes.
A feasible evaluation method and evidence responsibilities make the inter-team verification commitment specific and testable.
Interaction-level results expose which cross-team assumptions fail and which dependencies require correction.
Accurate cross-boundary links let affected teams locate the requirements, interfaces and evidence that require reconsideration.
The explicit system argument identifies the cross-team assumption or evidence gap that coordination must resolve for the claimed conclusion.
One problem identity, affected versions and residual disposition prevent cross-team handoffs from losing or duplicating the anomaly.
Scoped model authority, interoperability and version relationships make cross-team data exchange and reconciliation concrete.
Configuration-linked recurring results reveal incompatible assumptions and provide current shared evidence for dependency decisions.
